datapoints.label: MoE (small active params) vs dense of same total size — decode speedup on bandwidth-bound home hardware
datapoints.value_text: ~8x on DGX Spark (Qwen3-30B-A3B MoE 89 t/s vs Qwen3-32B dense 10.7 t/s, same ~30B total); ~15x on Strix Halo (30B-A3B MoE 70-100 t/s vs dense 70B ~5 t/s). Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound; MoE reads only active experts per token (~2.4-5B) while dense streams ALL weights every token.
datapoints.source_name: DandinPower llama.cpp DGX Spark bench report + DataHardware Strix Halo tok/s 2026
datapoints.notes: KEY MODELLING FACT for the calculator. DandinPower measures Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE, ~2.4B active/token) at 89.3 t/s vs Qwen3-32B (dense) at 10.7 t/s on the SAME DGX Spark = 8.3x from architecture alone at similar 30-32B total. Rule of thumb: gen speed ~= mem-bandwidth / bytes-read-per-token. gpt-oss-120b (116.8B total / 5.1B active, 128-expert MoE top-4) is why a '120B' model runs at ~55-60 t/s on 273 GB/s hardware while a dense 70B crawls at ~3-5 t/s. Cross-checked at https://datahardware.ai/blog/strix-halo-tokens-per-second-2026 (15x on Strix Halo).

datapoints.value_text: ~55-60 t/s at shallow context (d0=60.6, d4096=54.1, d16384=47.5, d32768=40.6). NVIDIA official 55.4; llama.cpp maintainers ~58.7. Vary by build/context.

datapoints.notes: MoE, MXFP4 (~59 GiB, 116.8B params, 5.1B active). Single-stream decode. Falls off with context depth (60.6 @ d0 -> 40.6 @ d32768). NVIDIA official llama.cpp figure 55.37 t/s. This matches the calculator's existing gpt_oss_120b single=60 (confidence medium) — CONFIRMED and can be raised to high confidence. Memory bandwidth 273 GB/s is the ceiling. Dual-Spark does NOT help single-stream decode (interconnect latency lowers it to ~47 t/s).

datapoints.label: DGX Spark (GB10) — gpt-oss-120b (MoE) BATCHED aggregate decode (vLLM, high concurrency)

datapoints.source_name: Dendro Logic — DGX Spark concurrency benchmark (gpt-oss-120b, vLLM, ASUS GX10/GB10)

Workload: ~1500 in / 400 out tokens.

datapoints.label: RTX 5090 (32GB) — gpt-oss-120b (MoE) single-stream decode
datapoints.value_text: ~30 t/s at zero context via llama.cpp CPU-MoE offload (--n-cpu-moe 21). Does NOT fit in 32GB VRAM at Q4 — requires offloading MoE layers to system RAM, so bandwidth-limited by CPU RAM, not the 1792 GB/s VRAM.
datapoints.notes: CRITICAL: gpt-oss-120b (~60GB MXFP4) does NOT fit a 32GB 5090. It only runs via MoE-layer CPU offload, which caps decode at ~30 t/s (bottlenecked by host DRAM bandwidth, ~8GB min VRAM). This is why UMA boxes (128GB unified) beat the 5090 for large MoE despite the 5090's 6.5x higher VRAM bandwidth. A 5090 is NOT a good host for the calculator's default gpt_oss_120b model.
